operative_clauses.original_operative_text: Section 1. The United States Civil Service Commission is hereby designated and empowered to exercise, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President, the following:

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 1 (lead-in)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (1) The authority vested in the United States Civil Service Commission by Section 605 of the Federal Employees Pay Act of 1945, 59 Stat. 304 (5 U.S.C. 945), to issue, subject to the approval of the President, regulations necessary for the administration of certain provisions of that Act insofar as the Act affects officers and employees in or under the executive branch of the Government.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 1(1)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (2) The authority vested in the President by Section 203(f) of the Annual and Sick Leave Act of 1951, 65 Stat. 680 (5 U.S.C. 2062(f)), to prescribe regulations governing the granting of leave of absence as described in that Section.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 1(2)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (3) Except as to Presidential appointees, the authority vested in the President (A) by Section 204 of the Act of June 30,1932, 47 Stat. 404, to exempt from automatic separation from the service under that Section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires, and (B) by Section 5(c) of the Civil Service Retirement Act, 70 Stat. 748 (5 U.S.C. 2255(c)), to exempt from automatic separation from the service under Section 5 of that Act any employee when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 1(3)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: Sec. 2. The Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission is hereby designated and empowered to exercise, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President, the authority vested in the President by Section 304(e) of the Government Employees' Incentive Awards Act, 68 Stat. 1113 (5 U.S.C. 2123(e)), to determine the activity primarily benefiting, or the various activities benefiting, from any suggestion, invention, superior accomplishment, or other personal effort of any civilian officer or employee of the Government which constitutes the basis of any Presidential award or honorary recognition made or granted under Section 304(b) of that Act (5 U.S.C. 2123(b)).

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 2

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: Sec. 3. The following are hereby superseded:

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 3 (lead-in)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (1) Part II of Executive Order No. 10530 of May 10, 1954.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 3(1)
American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 3(2)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (3) Section 5 of Executive Order No. 10800 of January 15, 1959.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 3(3)
American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 3(4)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (5) So much of Section 2 of Executive Order No. 10903 of January 9, 1961, as added paragraph (e) to Section 2 of Executive Order No. 10530 of May 10,1954.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 3(5)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (a) Unless inappropriate, references in this Order to any statute or to any provision of any statute shall be deemed to include references thereto as amended from time to time.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 4(a)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (b) Unless inappropriate, any reference in any Executive order to any Executive order which is superseded by this Order, or to any Executive order provision so superseded, shall hereafter be deemed to refer to this Order or to the provision of Section 1 or Section 2 of this Order, if any, which corresponds to the superseded provision.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); Sec. 4(b)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: Sec. 5. All actions heretofore taken by the President or by his delegates in respect of the matters affected by Sections 1 and 2 of this Order and in force at the time of the issuance of this Order, including any regulations prescribed or approved by the President or by his delegates in respect of such matters, shall, except as they may be inconsistent with the provisions of this Order, remain in effect until amended, modified, or revoked pursuant to the authority conferred by this Order unless sooner terminated by operation of law.
